name: Tearout - Machine-gun bass layers
description: Reference checklist for a layered tearout gun bass: gritty sine sub, mid body, short click/transient and a tonal layer, glued and resampled into one hit. Not executable.

manual.instruction: Build four separate layers: a gritty sine sub with noise and tube drive, a mid-range bass body, a short percussion transient EQ'd at its peak, and a tonal layer.
manual.verify: Each layer has one job and the sub is clean enough to survive on a club system.
manual.why: MOONBOY's tearout method splits sub, bass, transient and tonal layers before gluing them.

manual.instruction: Give the sub a fast falling pitch envelope. On the body, use a second wavetable, a retriggered triplet LFO and a little noise for the click; keep the high click short and remove its low end so it does not clash with the sub.
manual.verify: The hit has a downward gunshot shape rather than one static bass note.
manual.why: Code: Pandorum calls the sub pitch fall crucial to the machine-gun identity and builds a separate short click layer.

manual.instruction: Add a comb or steep low-pass filter, convolution and distortion to the body. Cut low end before distortion for definition, or leave some for crackle; make tone and length macros so the same patch yields several gun variations.
manual.verify: The body has a metallic, filtered crack and the variations stay in the same family.
manual.why: Code: Pandorum uses comb filtering, convolution, a steep driven low-pass, distortion and tone/length macros for the chain-gun foundation.

manual.instruction: For the transient, shape a gun-like LFO that opens instantly and falls. Try an FM layer that starts high and drops low, then rises; Wheysted reverses the usual upward pitch movement for a harder impact.
manual.verify: The front of the hit is instantly present and the tail falls away instead of swelling.
manual.why: Wheysted's tearout-gun tutorial uses a fast transient LFO, pitch bend and reversed FM movement.

manual.instruction: Group the layers and glue them with OTT, saturation and glue compression. Match the group level, then resample the whole hit so further filtering and chopping are cheap.
manual.verify: The layers read as one sound and the resampled hit keeps its transient.
manual.why: MOONBOY groups the four layers, processes them together and resamples; Dripment uses a repeatable OTT/Saturator/EQ/clipper loud rack.

manual.instruction: Make variations from the resample: a band-passed phone-filter fill before the drop, a disperser for a watery transient, or a pitch-shifted copy. Keep reverb off the sub and check the gun in mono.
manual.verify: The variations build tension without smearing the drop; the sub stays centered.
manual.why: MOONBOY uses filtered fills and a disperser on resampled basses; Oddprophet keeps the sub out of the convolution path.

notes: Sources: MOONBOY, 'HOW TO TEAROUT DUBSTEP (Marauda, Kai Wachi, Excision)' (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nApsgDWSQ7Y); Code: Pandorum, 'MACHINE GUN BASS DESIGN' (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sk--QbE_TM0); Wheysted Music, 'SERUM TEAR-OUT GUN BASS TUTORIAL' (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KkXF4T_WPbY); Dripment, '2 TEAROUT Serum 2 BASS ROUTINES' (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NRfK34KZIf8). Transcript summaries, not quotes. Reference-only because the engine cannot build, resample or verify these patches.
